hints.title: Divisor Structure
hints.text: A number has exactly two proper divisors if and only if it is the square of a prime number p, giving proper divisors 1 and p.

hints.title: Upper Bound on Base Primes
hints.text: Because r is at most one billion, candidate primes p only need to be enumerated up to the integer square root of r which is thirty-one thousand six hundred twenty-two.

hints.title: Sieve Enumeration
hints.text: Use the sieve of Eratosthenes up to the square root limit. Count squares falling within the interval and subtract from total interval length.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Sieve up to sqrt(r) dominates execution.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Factoring every integer individually takes O((r - l) * sqrt(r)) resulting in timeout.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(sqrt(r)) memory stores the boolean sieve array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that special numbers are prime squares and uses Eratosthenes sieve.
